intro: Step into Old Mardin, a historic town in Mardin province whose fabric belongs to the 12th–19th century. The town is terraced down the slope above the Mesopotamian plain, and here carved limestone madrasas, mosques and Syriac churches stand side by side. Take a breath and enjoy the view.
history: Mardin is terraced down the south face of a limestone ridge that commands the Mesopotamian plain. Each house's roof serves as the courtyard of the one above. The result? The whole town enjoys an unbroken view and natural ventilation. The fabric of the town was shaped under the Artuqids, and here mosque, madrasa, church and monastery stand on the same street. Look closely at the walls: carved stone is the region's distinctive art.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Great Mosque, the Zinciriye Madrasa and the Kasımiye Madrasa, and then the Deyrulzafaran Monastery and the Kırklar Church.
facts: Did you know? The long pool in the courtyard of the Kasımiye Madrasa was designed to describe a human life: water rises from its source, rests in the basin, and flows away. The town is terraced so that each house's roof is the courtyard of the one above, giving every house an unbroken view over the plain. Mosque, madrasa, church and monastery stand on the same street, and the Syriac monastery of Deyrulzafaran has been in the same place for 1,500 years.
outro: This brings our tour of Old Mardin to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking these terraces with us, and enjoy your visit.
